value: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (1996-1998). AP-42, Compilation of Air Pollutant Emission Factors, Fifth Edition, Volume I: Stationary Point and Area Sources, Chapter 1 External Combustion Sources, Sections 1.1 Bituminous and Subbituminous Coal Combustion (9/98), 1.3 Fuel Oil Combustion (9/98), 1.4 Natural Gas Combustion (7/98), 1.5 Liquefied Petroleum Gas Combustion (10/96), 1.6 Wood Waste Combustion in Boilers (9/98), 1.7 Lignite Combustion (9/98). Office of Air Quality Planning and Standards, Research Triangle Park, NC.

EMISSION-FACTOR REFERENCE, not a technology source: belongs in source-details_reference.csv. Only GHG factors (CO2, CH4, N2O, plus TOC where it is the printed basis for CH4) loaded to _factors.csv; criteria pollutants skipped. Units kept as printed: lb/10^3 gal (oil, LPG), lb/10^6 scf (gas), lb/ton (coal, lignite, wood). Locators are PDF page numbers, which equal the printed AP-42 page numbers. Coal (Table 1.1-20) and lignite (Table 1.7-1) CO2 are carbon-content equations (72.6 x %C) plus defaults. No boiler thermal efficiency figures are printed in any of the six sections. Files kept as <stem>-s1-N.pdf (coal as -s1-1).

(1) Heating values differ per section and are not always labelled HHV/LHV: gas 1,020 Btu/scf gross; oil 140/150 MMBtu/10^3 gal; LPG 91.5 propane/102 butane MMBtu/10^3 gal; coal 26.0 MMBtu/ton; wood 9.0 MMBtu/ton = 4,500 Btu/lb HHV at 50% moisture; lignite 6,500 Btu/lb in text (x0.077) vs 16 MMBtu/ton in table footnotes (x0.0625), inconsistent. (2) Wood CO2 is biogenic. (3) Coal Table 1.1-19 N2O footnotes e/f/h are absent from the PDF copy. (4) Natural gas N2O has uncontrolled 2.2 vs low-NOx 0.64 lb/10^6 scf. (5) Wood CH4 appears twice: 0.1 lb/ton stoker (Table 1.6-3) and 1.12E-02 lb/ton (speciated Table 1.6-4). (6) Lignite has no CH4 factor; N2O only for FBC. (7) Most CH4/N2O ratings are D/E.
